_doc: Hand-written source of semantics/axioms.json (built by semantics/tools/build_semantics.py, which adds violating_findings from src/finding_classes.json and relied_on_by from objects.json). Product pin 3eaa79cf; every source path is at the pin.

axioms.name: One writer per fact
axioms.rule: Each kind of stored fact has one owning mechanism, and every write of that fact goes through it, with the owner's checks.
axioms.formal: for every store s and every write step w: writes(w) contains s => w is a method of owner(s), or w calls owner(s) with owner(s)'s guards
axioms.repair_note: SYS-I1 named the owner but not the guards; a writer that writes the owned store directly, or calls the owner while skipping its checks (identity, mark, kind), is the same defect (F-0602, F-0603, F-1107).

axioms.name: Graph and tenant scope
axioms.rule: A command scoped to a graph or tenant reads and changes only that graph's or tenant's content; an all-graphs read is the union of each graph's own answer; every predicate that names a tenant (erase, liveness, record match) names the same content.
axioms.formal: answer(cmd, g) = answer(cmd, restrict(state, g)); effect(cmd, g) leaves restrict(state, h) unchanged for h != g; erase_pred(t) = live_pred(t) = match_pred(t)
axioms.repair_note: SYS-I2 covered answers only. Extended to writes (F-1503, F-0507), to the all-graphs union rule (CONTEXT.md:38-43, F-0209) and to the three target predicates whose difference is the root of F-1304/F-1305 (P-1310 refuted, TRUST.md).

axioms.name: Explicit, inert refusals
axioms.rule: A refused or failed command leaves every store as it was (the caller's own earlier writes included) and says why, with a code of the product's error family; a failure is never reported as success, as no rows, or as another error.
axioms.formal: outcome(cmd) = refused(code) => state' = state and code in ErrorFamily(cmd)
axioms.repair_note: Merges SYS-I3 (changes nothing) and SYS-I9 (says why), as the playbook's 'explicit, recorded refusals'. Extended: the caller's earlier writes in its own transaction are part of 'every store' (F-C0702, F-0409), and a silent drop or a misreported error class is a refusal that does not say why (F-0307, F-0817, F-C1602).

axioms.name: All or none across stores
axioms.rule: A command that writes several stores writes all of them or none: it is one transaction, or a sequence whose every intermediate state is named and recoverable.
axioms.formal: for every execution of cmd ending at a quiescent point: delta(state) in {full_effect(cmd), empty}
axioms.repair_note: Unchanged in substance; units sent to a server (Bolt explicit transactions, HTTP tx commit, FHIR event writes) are commands too (F-1601, F-1610, F-1609).

axioms.name: History only grows
axioms.rule: The ledger's records and revisions are only appended; a saved record changes only into its tombstone, and the head never moves back.
axioms.formal: for every step: records'[k] in {records[k], tomb(records[k])} for k <= head, and head' >= head
axioms.repair_note: Adds 'the head never moves back', which a replacing restore violates (F-1801).

axioms.name: At most once per retry key
axioms.rule: A request repeated with the same retry key (or the same business identity) takes effect at most once; a repeat gets the first answer without any further effect, or a clear refusal.
axioms.formal: count(effects(key)) <= 1; replay(key) => delta(state) = empty (post-commit effects included)
axioms.repair_note: Extended from the ledger key to every retry layer (HTTP client resend, server re-run) and to post-commit effects (F-1306, F-C1703, F-C1604).

axioms.name: A governed change is recorded with it
axioms.rule: While the ledger governs a kind of content, every change of that content is saved in the same transaction as its record; a write that cannot be recorded is refused in strict mode.
axioms.formal: ledger on and kind governed: delta(content) != empty <=> a record of exactly that delta commits in the same transaction
axioms.repair_note: Adds both directions: no record without its change (F-0511, F-1105) and no unrecorded change while strict (F-0301, F-1108).

axioms.name: Derived stores match or say they are stale
axioms.rule: A store built from other stores either equals its derivation from their committed content or carries a staleness signal every reader checks; a rolled-back or interrupted source write never leaves a derived store current and wrong.
axioms.formal: stamp(D) = token => D = f(committed(S)); every write of S moves token or updates D in S's transaction
axioms.repair_note: Adds committed content (rollback, F-0402, F-C0401) and the reader's obligation to check the signal (F-0906).

axioms.name: One install, one schema, one version per namespace
axioms.rule: A namespace holds one install of the product under one recorded schema; setup is idempotent, reports every failure, never touches objects outside that schema, and code runs only against the version it expects.
axioms.formal: recorded_schema(ns) fixed after first setup; setup;setup = setup; touched(setup) within schema(ns) union manifest(legacy)
axioms.repair_note: Adds idempotence, the failure report and the version gate (F-0102, F-0103, F-0107).

axioms.name: Removal reaches every store and copy
axioms.rule: Erasure followed by redaction removes a target's content from every store that holds it, every derived store and every copy the product makes (indexes, quarantine, snapshots, history text, retry keys), or the receipt names exactly what remains.
axioms.formal: after erase(t); redact(t) succeeds: for every store s in Stores (inventory complete): content(s, t) = empty, or s in receipt.remaining
axioms.repair_note: New. SYS-D26/D27 define erasure and redaction; no SYS axiom stated their reach. Spec 256 SC-001 and FR-008 (receipt) are its intent sources.

axioms.name: Conflicting commands serialize
axioms.rule: Commands whose footprints overlap behave as if run one at a time: each takes the lock that guards what it reads and writes, a marker is set before the first effect it guards, and only its owner clears it.
axioms.formal: every reachable history of overlapping commands is equivalent to some serial order of them
axioms.repair_note: New. Implicit in ADR-0013 (head lock), ADR-0011/0012 (writer lock, generations) and spec 256 FR-006; every S1 race finding (F-1201, F-1302, F-1303, F-C1201) violates it.

axioms.name: Truthful outcomes and committed observations
axioms.rule: A command's reported outcome equals its effect: success means the whole effect happened and is kept, counts and receipts report what was done; a read changes no stored state except derived caches, and a read or an archive shows a state some serial order of committed commands produced.
axioms.formal: outcome(cmd) = ok(r) => effect(cmd) complete and durable and r = report(effect); read: delta(primary state) = empty and answer from some committed serial state
axioms.repair_note: New. The durability half is intent-undecided (F-C1102: no IVG document states a durability premise). Read purity (a read writes no primary state) is part of it (F-C1001).

axioms.name: Least capability
axioms.rule: A caller can do only what its key and role allow: a read-only caller changes nothing, a missing or wrong key is refused before any effect, and no entry point hands a caller a capability beyond the product's API (server files, raw SQL or code text).
axioms.formal: role(caller) = read_only => delta(state) = empty; keys_on and not key_ok => refused before effect
axioms.repair_note: New. Intent: docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md section 5, spec 253 FR-011.

axioms.name: Accepted work progresses
axioms.rule: Work the product accepts (a queue entry, a run, a session) finishes or is reported failed under fair scheduling: no entry starves, no run restarts forever, no resource stays held after its holder ends.
axioms.formal: under weak fairness of the worker: pending(e) leads-to done(e) or failed(e)
axioms.repair_note: New. Progress premises are TRUST.md rows (fair scheduling, operator re-runs); the axiom states what the product must do under them.

exceptions.name: DDL after commit
exceptions.rule: EraseGraph drops routed vector tables after its transaction commits; a failure there leaves empty tables, not content.

exceptions.name: PurgeAll reset
exceptions.rule: PurgeAll is a test and admin reset of the whole ledger, outside the growth rule.

exceptions.name: Post-commit properties
exceptions.rule: Post-commit properties are written by the client after the ledger commit, outside its transaction (by design; their replay is F-1306).

exceptions.name: Vectors are not ledgered
exceptions.rule: Vector writes never pass through the ledger and no revision holds a vector (VEC-B1.2).

exceptions.name: Route cache window
exceptions.rule: An engine may reuse a route it read up to 30 s ago without asking the registry (VEC-T2.13); missing routes are never cached.

exceptions.name: Interned snapshot has no graph dimension
exceptions.rule: The interned snapshot gives the default graph's answer only while no named graph has an edge (documented).

exceptions.name: Tombstone keeps shape and digest
exceptions.rule: A tombstone keeps seq, ordinal, op kind, entity kind and a SHA-256 digest of the replaced record (ADR-0013); the digest is not content.

exceptions.name: Monotone counters survive rollback
exceptions.rule: $Increment counters and version tokens are not undone by a rollback (E-INCR); they only mark staleness, so a rolled-back increment is safe.

exceptions.name: Legacy objects kept until removed
exceptions.rule: 4.5.x objects outside the IVG Schema stay in place, frozen and unused, until an operator removes them from the fixed manifest.

exceptions.name: Algorithm runs read without isolation
exceptions.rule: Algorithms read the edges with no lock; a write during a long run can give a mix of old and new edges (ALG-P6; the concurrency contract of Neo4j GDS, spec 162 FR-021).

exceptions.name: Undeclared adjacency or label index
exceptions.rule: Where the adjacency or label index is not declared on its table, only the engine's own writers and a rebuild keep it; any other write leaves it stale, and its declaration flag (Graph.KG.Adjacency.Indexed) is the signal readers must check (CONTEXT.md, Adjacency Index).

contract_clauses._doc: Clauses a requirement may trace to besides an axiom: the IRIS environment contract (iris-contract/CONTRACT.md, ids E-*/X-*), the domain contract (3.3a-domain-contract: DC-REPLAY) and each module's functional contract (DC-FUNC-NN: the module's L1 model in its D-1 crate, which defines what its commands compute; a trace to it says the requirement is a functional rule of that module, not an instance of a universal axiom).

domain.rule: The fold of the committed records (replay) equals the governed content of the store.
